items.title: After Undo of a project made with Take it over, the next New project on that repository gets no offer and takes nothing over
items.what_the_person_sees: New project on a repository whose main names "Kite club" > Take it over, then Undo on Changes. A second New project on the same repository is made at once with no offer (no Work together, no Take it over), although main still names "Kite club". Its Overview has no line about the other project and its docs keep Kite club's marker, so another Forerunner is still offered "Kite club". From then on this computer treats the repository as free for any New project, even if someone works on Kite club again (the 14-day rule is skipped).
items.evidence: live4:L4-github-2. /tmp/frbench/live4/github/evidence/a01-takeover.json, a03-undo.json, a04-takeover-brief.json (createStatus 201, noOffer true), a04-db-projects-after-undo-and-second-create.jsonl (the removed row 01a1e7fd keeps took_over [01a1be66]; the new row 01a1e7ff has none), a05.json (repositoryElsewhere null), c1-a-before-approve.json (main's marker names Kite club); screenshot /tmp/frbench/live4/github/evidence/a-home1/steps/16-a04-takeover-brief-no-offer.png; module repro /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-github-2/repro.mts.
items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/sources/repository-use.ts:353-361 RepositoryIndex.knows(id) loops over every row, removed ones included, and returns true when any row's settings.took_over.projects names the id (:358). verdictOf then skips that id (:571 `if (index.knows(id)) continue;`) and answers {kind:"free"} (:574); overviewOf returns null on it (:988). project.create's Undo (packages/commands/src/commands/project.ts:398-411) archives the row with removed_name and keeps settings.took_over.
items.fix_sketch: In RepositoryIndex.knows keep `row(id)` for any status, and inside the loop skip a removed project (`if (isRemovedProject(p)) continue;`, already imported) before the projectIdsOf and tookOverOf checks: a removed project uses nothing (ADR 0117 point 2), so neither its take-over nor its joined ids make an id "known". A joined project (archived with joined_into) still counts through its keeper. The "removed" verdict (the marker names the person's own removed project; run C session lead decision 14, took_over with removed true) is unchanged: verdictOf finds it through index.row before knows is asked. project.ts's Undo is not changed: the index fix also covers rows stored this way already. ADR 0117 point 2 reads "an id a project here (not a removed one) took over"; docs/maintainers/runtime.md "One repository, one project".
items.test_boundary: Real-daemon case in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts, describe "l4-github-link, run L4", MemoryGitHost: o/kite's main carries the marker {project: KITE, name: "Kite club"}. client.createProject on o/kite answers 409 repository_used_elsewhere with canTakeOver true; with takeOver {projects:[KITE]} it answers 201; Undo that change through the Changes undo route; createProject with a brief on o/kite again must answer 409 naming "Kite club" with canWorkTogether and canTakeOver true (today 201); a project on o/kite whose copy's marker names KITE gets a non-null repositoryElsewhere from GET /projects/:id (today null); the same after composing twice. Unit twin in packages/runtime/test/repository-use.test.ts: verdictOf/check with a removed row whose took_over names KITE answers "elsewhere", never "free".
items.notes: Placed first in its area: it breaks the owner's D1 and D9 (one repository, one project; Work together first; a take-over only for a project nobody uses) after an ordinary Undo. The model plays no part. knows() came in with 9f4b2b8 (d1109-onerepo-link). Session lead decision 14 ("a project removed by Undo of its creation frees its repository") covers the marker that names the removed project itself, not a third project's marker the removed one had taken over: this fix keeps that default.

items.title: Take it over opens no docs pull request when an old fr/docs-scaffold branch is on GitHub, or adds no take-over line to this project's own open scaffold pull request, and no screen says so
items.what_the_person_sees: Take it over on forerunner-sandbox: the project opens normally, but no pull request appears on GitHub and the repository keeps naming "Kite club". The Overview has no line, Docs says "8 of 8 present", and the line under Take it over ("The repository then names this project") did not come true. When this project's own scaffold pull request is already open at the take-over (C4L-2), that pull request gets no take-over line and its marker conflicts with main's when it is merged.

items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:875 scaffoldInCopy calls this.checkout(project, target, "fr/docs-scaffold", { ours }) with no `fresh`, so checkout (:1249-1254) starts the copy from origin/fr/docs-scaffold whenever that ref exists, here a closed pull request's branch carrying a third project's marker. mark() (:1427-1440) keeps that marker (status other_project, only a WARN log), scaffoldDocs finds every doc present, so nothing is written: no commit, no push (:921, never forced), no pull request. The outcome (prUrl null, marker other_project) is only recorded: create-project.ts:192 -> scaffoldProjectDocs (:204-216) ignores it; compose.ts:4916-4924 repositoryTakeOver.writeMarker sets failed only when the scaffold throws; no screen reads marker.status. writeSessionStatus already passes `fresh: async (open) => !open` (:983) and pushes with `force: !existingPr` (:998). C4L-2: with this project's own scaffold pull request open, the run comments only the missing docs (:922-928) and commits the replaced marker on top of the old branch instead of rebuilding it on the default branch.
items.fix_sketch: 1) scaffoldInCopy passes `fresh: async (open) => !open` and pushes with `force: !existingPr`, as writeSessionStatus: with no open scaffold pull request the branch starts from origin/<default branch>. Data rule: force only over a branch whose head is the head of a closed or merged pull request (GitHub keeps it under refs/pull/N/head) or that carries this install's own mark; any other fr/docs-scaffold on GitHub (someone's own branch) is never overwritten, and the outcome says why no pull request opened. Another project's open pull request stays `foreign` (W15-01: never written to or commented on). 2) C4L-2: a take-over while this project's own scaffold pull request is open rebuilds that branch on the default branch under the copy's lock, writes the replaced marker, force-pushes this project's own branch and comments tookOverLine on the pull request (ADR 0117's amendment). 3) Said where the person reads the take-over: compose.ts writeMarker returns failed (or a new notOpened) when prUrl is null and nothing was written, so repo.take_over answers tookOverNoPullRequestSentence; POST /projects with takeOver records the same on the row and the Overview's take-over line reads that GitHub still names "Kite club" because the docs pull request could not be opened; Docs does not read "8 of 8 present" as if the take-over had landed. 4) Sibling (validation rule 8): packages/runtime/src/session/intake.ts:2521-2533 writeDocsToRepository starts fr/intake-<id>-docs from the default branch when no pull request is open but pushes without force (`force: !!existingPr`), so an old branch of the same name refuses the push: same rule. 5) docs/maintainers/runtime.md (the scaffold branch's start rule), ADR 0117 dated amendment.
items.test_boundary: Composed daemon test in packages/runtime/test/docs-scaffold.test.ts (MemoryGitHost and a bare repository, app.request), in the OR-06/OR-15 describe: o/kite's main has the doc set and Kite club's marker, and an fr/docs-scaffold branch not in main carries a third project's marker with its pull request closed. POST /projects without takeOver answers 409; with takeOver {projects:[KITE]} 201. Expect exactly one open pull request on fr/docs-scaffold whose body has the take-over line, its marker names the new project, main is an ancestor of the branch and the diff to main is only .forerunner/project.json (today: no pull request). Second case (C4L-2): this project's own scaffold pull request open, then repo.take_over through POST /commands: the branch is rebuilt on main with the replaced marker and the pull request gets the take-over line. Third: a host refusal at the push: repo.take_over's sentence reads 'Took over o/kite from "Kite club" here, but the docs pull request that names this project could not be opened, so GitHub still names "Kite club".' and the Overview line says so (real-daemon case through client.project, describe "l4-github-link, run L4"). A remote branch that is no pull request's head is not overwritten.
items.notes: Same root cause from two sources: the scaffold branch is not started from the default branch (L4-github-1 with no open pull request; C4L-2 with this project's own open one), so they are one item. Severity major, not blocker: the project works in the app, but the take-over's promise silently does not happen on GitHub, and an old head branch of a closed pull request is GitHub's default. Wider effect (reasoned from the code, not run): any new project on a repository with an old fr/docs-scaffold branch that lacks some docs would add them on top of the old commit and open a pull request carrying another project's marker. The brief path (PR #50) was not affected: the intake writes its own fr/intake-<id>-docs branch.

items.title: Settings lets a Work-together project turn on the status pull request and promises one, but none ever opens
items.what_the_person_sees: On a project made with Work together, Settings offers "Status pull request" with Change; turning it on reads back "each session's status goes to the repository as one pull request, docs: project status, which you merge when you like". After a session the log says "Created the project status in docs/status.md, kept in the app." and Docs says "Kept in the app: you work on "Kite flyers" together, so GitHub's copy is left as it is."; no pull request ever opens.
items.evidence: live4:L4-l3-10 (l3 journey screenshots 08-kt-new-offer, 11-kt-statuspr-after; l3a home app-status/docs/status.md; the sandbox had no open pull request after the session); live4-step:l3:LC-L3.L3-github-6 (observed: the status words are right, no status pull request because the project is shared, although Settings said it would go to GitHub).
items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/daemon/settings-view.ts:315-325 shows the "Status pull request" row with Change whenever onHostRepository(p), never asking isTogether; packages/commands/src/commands/settings.ts:403-418 status_pull_request's effect ignores the project and settings.set has no together refusal, so Settings, chat and voice get the same false read-back. The behaviour it contradicts is right: packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:968 keeps a together project's status in the app whatever the setting (D9).
items.fix_sketch: (a) At the command, so chat and voice get it too: settings.set status_pull_request=true on a together project (isTogether from @forerunner/runtime/sources/repository-words) is refused in one sentence with nothing written: 'You work on "Kite flyers" together with another Forerunner, so its status stays in the app (Docs, Status); no status pull request is opened.' (details {key, cause: "together"}); turning it off still acts. (b) settings-view.ts shows the row only when onHostRepository(p) && !isTogether(p), as C-57 hides it for a linked folder. (c) apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts mirrors both. (d) The user guide's "Working with someone on one repository" section and docs/maintainers (settings, docs).
items.test_boundary: Real-daemon case (describe "l4-github-link, run L4", or extend packages/runtime/test/onerepo-together.test.ts's two-home case): after Work together on o/kite, GET /settings has no project.status_pull_request row for the project; POST /commands settings.set {key:"status_pull_request", value:true, project} answers refused with the exact sentence, the change log gains no row and the setting is unchanged; the same through chat's settings_set tool (commands unit with the executor). UI test: SettingsPage on the fake daemon's together project shows no Change for Status pull request.
items.notes: The step LC-L3.L3-github-6 has no problem other than this finding, so it is one item. The owner's D9 ("a together project writes nothing to the repository") decides the behaviour; only Settings' promise is wrong (design section 5 rule 9). Model not involved.

items.title: A first plan whose reply leaves out the docs is taken without asking again, so the plan card has no decision line
items.what_the_person_sees: A new project's plan card normally shows "Decision: ..." (the drafted docs/decisions/0001) before Approve and start. If the model's first-plan reply leaves out "docs" entirely, the card shows no decision, the project gets only template docs and no decision record, and nothing asks the model again.
items.evidence: C2:CL-6 (leftovers-C2.json, d1109-onerepo-link's review). Code at 4cf11fd only.
items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/session/intake.ts:237-242 IntakeProposalBody has `docs: IntakeDocs.default({})` for both forms (OR-08 made it optional for the plan-only form); parse at :821 then accepts a first-plan reply without docs, although the first-plan rules (:1996-2013) ask for docs/decisions/0001-<slug>.md whose "Decision:" line the card shows. The cut-off retry advice (:811) tells the model to "leave docs out".
items.fix_sketch: The parse knows the form: in the first-plan form a reply without docs/decisions/0001-<slug>.md is refused with one problem line for the one retry, e.g. 'docs: the decision record is missing: write docs/decisions/0001-<slug>.md with the choice the brief points to; any standard doc you leave out is written from the template.'; the plan-only form keeps the default {}. The cut-off advice keeps the record and drops the rest: 'Write each doc in a few lines, or leave out the standard docs (Forerunner writes them from its templates), but keep docs/decisions/0001 short.' Both are model-facing text: assert them exactly. If the retry also lacks it, the card is filed without a decision line as today (no third call).
items.test_boundary: packages/runtime/test/intake.test.ts through the intake route with the stand-in model: a first-plan reply without docs makes the one retry, whose request carries the exact problem line; the second reply with the record lands a card whose decision line the Inbox shows (real-daemon client.inbox, describe "l4-github-link, run L4"); a plan-only (Add to) reply without docs is still taken at once; the cut-off advice's exact text.
items.notes: A prompt the app sends (the cut-off advice "leave docs out") makes the missing record likely, so this is a fix in the app, not model-only. intake.ts is shared: this area owns IntakeProposalBody, the parse and the retry/cut-off problem lines only.

items.title: The other-host refusal always names github.com, and the line under Take it over can pass 100 characters
items.what_the_person_sees: On an install set up for a GitHub Enterprise host, linking a repository elsewhere answers "Forerunner works with repositories on github.com, not <host>.", which is untrue there. With a 60-character project name in the marker, the line under Take it over ("The repository then names this project: choose it only if no Forerunner uses "<name>" now.") runs to about 125 characters (design section 5 rule 1: a consequence line is at most 100).
items.evidence: C2:CL-8 (leftovers-C2.json). AGENTS.md: nothing hardcoded to one host.
items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/sources/repository-words.ts:190-192 otherHostSentence hardcodes "github.com"; :180-182 takeOverLine quotes the marker's whole name.
items.fix_sketch: otherHostSentence takes the configured web host (from config.githubApiBase, "github.com" by default) from its callers. takeOverLine cuts the quoted name at a word (balancedCut with cutWords, about 30 characters) so the line stays at most 100 characters, or reads 'The repository then names this project. Choose it only if nobody uses "<name>" now.'.
items.test_boundary: UI test (apps/ui/test/onerepo-link.test.tsx) with a 60-character marker name: the line under Take it over is at most 100 characters and the name is whole or cut at a word; real-daemon or route case: an install whose API base is a GitHub Enterprise host refuses a github.com repository naming that host.

items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/session/dependent-branches.ts:208-232 mergedOnHost moves only the merged task's record and rebuilds what built on it; :234-243 closedOnHost moves A's record to left_to_you/"closed" without asking whether A's reviewed change reached the default branch through a merged dependent.
items.fix_sketch: When the watcher sees a pull request merged on GitHub (mergedOnHost) or a dependency closed (closedOnHost), each dependency of the merged one whose record is not merged is checked: if its reviewed head is an ancestor of the merge commit (git merge-base --is-ancestor in the copy under the copy's lock, or GitHub's compare), its record moves to merged with last_outcome "merged_through" and method null, sentence '#46 was closed, but its change reached main through #48.' (no migration: last_outcome is free text). Its row reads "Accepted · merged through #48"; one card says it with Take this work out (merged-actions' take-out of A's commits) and Keep it. Order-independent (whichever event the watcher reads first), idempotent across a restart; nothing is written to GitHub before the person presses. ADR 0111 point 4 replaced by a dated amendment; runtime.md.

decisions: A removed project uses nothing (ADR 0117 point 2): its take-over and joined ids no longer make an id known, so New project on its repository gets the offer again; a joined project's take-over still counts through its keeper; run C session lead decision 14 (a removed project frees its repository; the marker that names the removed project itself is replaced by the next project's first docs pull request) is kept. Why: the owner's D1 and D9.

The scaffold branch starts from the default branch whenever no scaffold pull request is open, as the status branch does; it is force-pushed only over a closed or merged pull request's branch or this install's own marked branch, never over anything else; another project's open pull request is never touched (W15-01). A take-over while this project's own scaffold pull request is open rebuilds that branch on the default branch before the replaced marker is written (ADR 0117's amendment). Why: GitHub keeps closed pull requests' head branches by default.

A take-over whose docs pull request did not open says so where the person reads the take-over (repo.take_over's sentence, the Overview's line, Docs), never "Took over ..." alone. Why: design section 5 rule 9.

A together project cannot turn on the status pull request: settings.set refuses in one sentence at the command (Settings, chat and voice alike) and Settings shows no switch for it. Why: D9 (a together project writes nothing to the repository).

The first-plan form needs the decision record; the cut-off advice keeps it short instead of dropping it; the plan-only form (Add to) writes no docs. Why: the plan card shows the decision before approval (design section 3.3).
Add to answers at once and plans in the background, as a new project's plan does; the Overview says the pending plan in one place (the banner with Open). Why: design sections 3.3 and 5 rule 10.
No possessive after a quoted name; a consequence line at most 100 characters; the configured host, never a hardcoded one. Why: design section 5 rules 1 and 6, run L3's L3-github-8, AGENTS.md.

decisions: A dependency whose reviewed change reached main through a pull request merged on GitHub is recorded as merged through it (state merged, last_outcome merged_through, no migration), in whatever order the watcher reads the two events and across a restart; one card says it with Take this work out and Keep it; nothing is written to GitHub before the person presses. Why: design section 5 rule 4; ADR 0111 point 4 left it for later.

Every merge card of a task closes when its pull request is closed on GitHub, as on a merge (ADR 0111 2026-11-15 point 3), Answered "Closed: #33 was closed on GitHub.". Why: U-028 (every option does what it says).

The press reads each pull request of the chain once before it answers (checks, mergeable state; the head for L4-creds-22) and refuses at once in the merge step's own words; nothing merges a pull request whose check failed. Why: run L3's L3-github-3 rule for every reason the merge step would refuse.

After a join the kept project lists the closing project's open status pull request (Open, Merge) whatever its own setting; the status writer still writes there only once the setting is on; the dialog names the status setting. Why: ADR 0117 point 3 ("one status pull request again") and the dialog's own promise that the pull requests move.
The dialog's open pull request count reads one predicate with the task row: a record closed on GitHub is not open.
Costs' runs and accepted runs of a task are the task's own, wherever its ledger rows are booked; money, totals and the other groupings stay the project's own ledger (BA-9, OJ-07).
A joined or removed project's page names itself in the header, never shows an internal folder, and its Last result says where its tasks went. Why: design sections 3.1 and 5 rules 3 and 4.
A merge the press found already made on GitHub reads "#59 was merged on GitHub already."; only Forerunner's own reads "Merged #59.". Why: ADR 0111 point 3.
